item.text:
**Verdict:** No.

Putin’s 2023 rule used digital controls and administrative harassment to constrain political freedom. The strongest evidence is the expanded electronic draft system, surveillance of activists, foreign-agent designations, and harassment of election monitors and independent media. I found no credible 2023 evidence that he meaningfully refrained from these tools.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Short claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Russia: 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | [link](https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia) | The report says authorities further restricted media, jailed antiwar protesters and opposition figures, forced NGO closures, and opened 844 criminal cases for antiwar expression. It also says the “discrediting the military” laws were used widely and indiscriminately. | 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.3 |
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023) | Freedom House says Russian authorities used excessive force against anti-war protests, criminalized dissent, and maintained a highly repressive security environment. It also describes a controlled media environment and a subservient judiciary, which fits administrative and digital repression rather than restraint. | 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.3, 4B.5 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023) | Freedom House says antiwar rallies were brutally suppressed, police used face recognition to track activists, and protest activity moved underground because opposition was criminalized. This is direct evidence of surveillance-enabled political control. | 4B.9, 4B.3, 4B.5 |
| Russia’s 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | [link](https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia) | The report says authorities jailed antiwar protesters and opposition figures and used harsh prison conditions against political prisoners. That is evidence of administrative harassment, not neutrality. | 4B.9, 4B.3 |
| Putin signs Russian law establishing electronic military draft records | Reuters | 14 Apr 2023 | [link](https://www.yahoo.com/news/putin-signs-russian-law-establishing-195445933.html) | Putin signed a law digitizing conscription records and electronic summonses, making mobilization more efficient and closing evasion loopholes. This is a concrete digital control tool that tightened state leverage over citizens. | 4B.9, 4B.2 |
| Russia’s anti-war media crackdown crosses new thresholds | Reuters | 21 Apr 2023 | [link](https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/analysisrussia-crosses-new-lines-in-crackdown-on-putins-enemies-2992615) | Reuters described security services and courts as crossing new thresholds in a campaign against perceived enemies, spies, and traitors. That supports a broader pattern of intimidation and administrative harassment against political freedom. | 4B.9, 4B.5, 4B.3 |
| Russia designates The Moscow Times newspaper a “foreign agent” | Reuters | 18 Nov 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-designates-the-moscow-times-newspaper-a-foreign-agent-3238256) | The Justice Ministry designated an independent newspaper a foreign agent, adding disclosure burdens and restrictions after it had already been blocked. This is classic administrative pressure on independent media. | 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5 |
| Russia arrests leader of vote monitoring group three weeks before regional polls | Reuters | 18 Aug 2023 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/russia-arrests-leader-of-vote-monitoring-group-three-weeks-before-regional-polls/1720660/) | Reuters said the arrest of Golos co-chair Grigory Melkonyants and raids on monitors’ homes appeared aimed at blocking scrutiny of the vote. That is administrative harassment of civil-society oversight. | 4B.9, 4B.3, 4B.4 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Looking back at 2023, Freedom House says electronic voting facilitated fraud and local autonomy had eroded, while the remaining municipal space was shrinking and tightly controlled. This is evidence that digital tools were part of political control, not freedom. | 4B.9, 4B.2, 4B.4 |
| Ministry of Justice of the Russian Federation FAQ on complaints and appeals | Ministry of Justice of the Russian Federation | 2023 | [link](https://minjust.gov.ru/ru/appeals/faq/589/) | The ministry says citizens can report crimes, investigators must register and review complaints, and complainants can appeal. This is formal procedure only, not a meaningful counterexample to surveillance or harassment. | 4B.9, 4B.4 |

**Search gap:** I found no credible 2023 evidence that Putin refrained from using surveillance, digital controls, or administrative harassment to limit political freedom. The closest counterevidence is only formal complaint procedure, not a real safeguard against the practices above.
